entries.value: "Credential store for base-studio-code — the METADATA half of a paired service credential (what it is, how it last behaved) at ~/.base-studio-code/secrets.db, over the shared bsc-json-store. The secret VALUE never enters this store: it stays in the OS keychain, and this crate only ever asks whether one is present."

lead: # build.rs parses the committed graph store directly — see crates/graph-materialize/build.rs.
# Tauri-free, like every other `bsc <noun>` store crate: the desktop app reaches it through the generic
# `bsc` bridge (console/bsc.rs) and a live session reaches the same store through the CLI.
sections.name: [build-dependencies]

lead: # THE SHARED CRATE ROOT — this crate owns no source file at all. See
# crates/graph-materialize/crate_root.rs; the crate's own docs come from its record.
# The shared verbatim-JSON-per-id store + CLI scaffold (#2158) — this crate supplies the credential
# nouns, the enriched `list`, and the write-time gate that keeps a secret OUT of the metadata store.
# Shared CLI scaffold (#1762): `CmdDoc` for the per-command help catalog + `resolve_store_path`.
# The ONE home-dir resolver (#1646) — the store dir resolves the same way every other store's does.
# The SECRET half. Mirrors src-tauri + crates/data's versions/features so all three processes reach
# the same platform store (#1194).
# THE LINUX BACKEND, and it is not optional.
# keyring 3 compiles a platform store only when its feature is on. With just the apple/windows
# features above, a Linux build gets NEITHER — and keyring's fallback is the in-process `mock` store,
# which accepts every write and is empty in the next process. Measured before this line existed:
# `bsc secret put github-acme` printed `{"stored":true}` and the very next `bsc secret list` reported
# `missing`. Nothing errors; the secret is simply gone, which is the worst possible way for a
# credential store to fail.
# `sync-secret-service` is the Secret Service (gnome-keyring / KWallet) — persistent across processes
# and logins, matching what apple-native and windows-native give the other two platforms.
# `linux-native` (kernel keyutils) was the alternative and is wrong here: it is session-scoped, so
# every stored credential would vanish at logout.
sections.name: [target.'cfg(target_os = "linux")'.dependencies]
